cues.en: Instructor: Well, the past two videos were a little bit dense on the math, so I wanted to change gears here a little bit and show an example of a simple regression.
cues.zh: 講師：前兩支影片的數學有點密集，所以想稍微換個方向，展示簡單迴歸的例子。

cues.en: So it turns out that simple regression is an official statistics term that doesn't just mean that it's like a really simple, cute, short example.
cues.zh: 其實，「簡單迴歸」是正式統計術語，不只是說這是個簡單、可愛、簡短的例子。

cues.en: And along the way, you're gonna learn more about concepts in regression that you learned in the past two videos, like the intercept and the statistical significance
cues.zh: 過程中，也會進一步了解前兩支影片學到的迴歸概念，例如截距、統計顯著性，

cues.en: and so on.
cues.zh: 等等。

cues.en: Okay, so what does simple regression mean?
cues.zh: 簡單迴歸是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, a simple regression, it has one dependent variable like our most regressions.
cues.zh: 與大部分迴歸一樣，有一個依變數。

cues.en: And depending on how you're counting it either has one independent variable or two.
cues.zh: 依計算方式，自變數可能算一個，也可能算兩個。

cues.en: So there's one independent variable that we are bringing into the model that our theory or our intuition suggests is important.
cues.zh: 有一個根據理論或直覺，認為重要而帶入模型的自變數。

cues.en: And then we have the other independent variable or the other column in the design matrix, which is the intercept.
cues.zh: 另一個自變數，或設計矩陣的另一欄，是截距。

cues.en: So yeah, there's two parameters of the model, and one of 'em is the intercept.
cues.zh: 所以模型有兩個參數，其中一個是截距。

cues.en: The other one is the independent variable that you bring into it.
cues.zh: 另一個則是你帶入的自變數。

cues.en: Okay, so that is the definition of a simple regression.
cues.zh: 這就是簡單迴歸的定義。

cues.en: So all simple regressions have this equation.
cues.zh: 所有簡單迴歸都有這個方程式。

cues.en: So it's Yi, let's see, I've labeled this here.
cues.zh: Yᵢ，這裡加上標示。

cues.en: So this is the Iif data point equals the intercept plus the beta coefficient, and the independent variable for the iif data value
cues.zh: 第 i 個資料點等於截距，加上 beta 係數乘以第 i 筆資料的自變數，

cues.en: and the iif error or residual or innovation term, whatever you want to call this little epsilon character here.
cues.zh: 再加上第 i 個誤差、殘差，或創新項，不管怎麼稱呼這個小 epsilon。

cues.en: And so again, we can rewrite the equation solving for epsilon, and that says epsilon is equal to, so the residual is equal to the observed data
cues.zh: 同樣可以改寫，解出 epsilon，表示殘差等於觀察資料，

cues.en: minus the model predicted data for this particular data point.
cues.zh: 減去模型對這個特定資料點的預測。

cues.en: So the I here is I write out innovation, the observed data minus the model predicted data.
cues.zh: 這裡的 i，我寫成 innovation，也就是觀察資料減去模型預測資料。

cues.en: So here's our research question.
cues.zh: 研究問題如下。

cues.en: Does the amount of sleep affect how much money people spend when they go food shopping?
cues.zh: 睡眠量，是否影響人們買食物時花多少錢？

cues.en: So it seems like a pretty reasonable question to ask.
cues.zh: 這似乎是合理的問題。

cues.en: Here's our experiment.
cues.zh: 實驗如下。

cues.en: We go to a market and we ask 10 randomly selected people to tell us the number of hours they slept the previous night and to tell us their total shopping bills,
cues.zh: 到市場，隨機選 10 個人，請他們告訴我們前一晚睡幾小時，以及總購物帳單，

cues.en: so how much money they spent on food.
cues.zh: 也就是買食物花了多少錢。

cues.en: Now, to make things a little more interesting, because this is a little bit of a boring experiment, so to make it more interesting, we are going to do this experiment in the beautiful island
cues.zh: 因為實驗有點無聊，為了更有趣，我們要在美麗的島國

cues.en: country of Fiji, which is located in the South Pacific.
cues.zh: 斐濟進行，它位於南太平洋。

cues.en: I am fortunate to have been there for a couple weeks, many years ago.
cues.zh: 很多年前，我很幸運地在那裡待過幾週。

cues.en: It's a beautiful, beautiful place, and I hope to go back someday.
cues.zh: 那裡非常漂亮，希望有一天能再去。

cues.en: And if you ever get the opportunity, you should definitely check it out or at least look at some pictures on Google.
cues.zh: 如果有機會，一定要去看看，或至少在 Google 看一些照片。

cues.en: It's a really beautiful, really great country.
cues.zh: 真的是非常美、非常棒的國家。

cues.en: Okay, they have dollars there, Fijian dollars.
cues.zh: 那裡使用元，也就是斐濟元。

cues.en: So here is the data from our experiment.
cues.zh: 這是實驗資料。

cues.en: In my imagination, I went back to Fiji and I asked people how much they slept and how much they spent on food.
cues.zh: 在想像中，我回到斐濟，問大家睡多久、買食物花多少錢。

cues.en: And now here the data are sorted according to how much they slept.
cues.zh: 這裡資料依睡眠時間排序。

cues.en: Here we see the graph of the data.
cues.zh: 這是資料圖。

cues.en: So just visually, even without doing any statistics, without doing any model fitting, we can already kind of guess what is going to happen here.
cues.zh: 光從視覺上，即使沒有統計、沒有擬合模型，也已經能大概猜到結果。

cues.en: It looks like there's a negative correlation between hours of sleep and money spent on food shopping.
cues.zh: 睡眠時數與食物購物花費，看起來有負相關。

cues.en: So it seems like the more people sleep, the less they spend on food shopping.
cues.zh: 似乎睡愈多，買食物花的錢愈少。

cues.en: Now of course, I just made up all of these numbers, like for everything else, but I think it's still important for me to remind you of that all the time.
cues.zh: 當然，和其他例子一樣，數字全是我編的，但仍應經常提醒你。

cues.en: So this is just my intuition.
cues.zh: 這只是我的直覺。

cues.en: I'm guessing, you know, when you don't sleep that much, you get a little bit more impulsive and so you maybe spending more on food or whatever is the reason.
cues.zh: 我猜，睡不多時會比較衝動，可能多買食物，或是其他原因。

cues.en: So now we have our visual intuition that tells us that there is a negative relationship here, but we need to test this statistically.
cues.zh: 現在視覺直覺告訴我們，這裡有負向關係，但需要統計檢定。

cues.en: We cannot just trust our visual intuition here.
cues.zh: 不能只相信視覺直覺。

cues.en: All right, so here we go with our model equation.
cues.zh: 這是模型方程式。

cues.en: And then here is the data expressed in a matrix vector equation, like what I showed before.
cues.zh: 這裡把資料寫成矩陣向量方程式，與之前展示的相同。

cues.en: So this is the design matrix.
cues.zh: 這是設計矩陣。

cues.en: The first column is the intercept, and the second column is the total amount of time that people slept.
cues.zh: 第一欄是截距，第二欄是睡眠總時間。

cues.en: And then we have the total amount of money that they spend food shopping.
cues.zh: 接著是買食物所花的總金額。

cues.en: And then here we have the two beta coefficients, the intercept.
cues.zh: 這裡有兩個 beta 係數，截距，

cues.en: And you can call this the slope.
cues.zh: 以及可以稱為斜率的這個係數。

cues.en: This is the linear relationship between number of hours slept and money.
cues.zh: 這是睡眠時數與金額的線性關係。

cues.en: Now, there's something I would like to point out here, and I also mentioned this in, I guess it was probably in the beginning of the section about hypothesis testing.
cues.zh: 有一件事想指出，假設檢定單元開頭大概也提過。

cues.en: It happens often in statistics and also in regression that which variable is the dependent variable and which variable is the independent variable
cues.zh: 統計與迴歸中，哪個是依變數，哪個是自變數，

cues.en: is mathematically ambiguous.
cues.zh: 經常在數學上不明確。

cues.en: So it could go either way.
cues.zh: 可以是任一方向。

cues.en: So I'm saying that the amount of time people slept is the independent variable and the, the amount of money that they spend is a dependent variable.
cues.zh: 這裡把睡眠時間當自變數，花費金額當依變數。

cues.en: Now, mathematically, you could actually swap these two columns here.
cues.zh: 數學上，其實可以交換這兩欄。

cues.en: You could say that we are going to predict how much people slept last night based on how much money they are spending today.
cues.zh: 可以說，根據今天花多少錢，預測昨晚睡多久。

cues.en: That is actually pretty acceptable.
cues.zh: 這其實可以接受。

cues.en: Now it might sound weird initially to say, we're trying to predict something that happened in the past based on what's happening now in the present.
cues.zh: 根據現在發生的事，預測過去發生的事，一開始聽起來可能很奇怪。

cues.en: But that would be, you know, that's kind of like a bit of the difference between the connotation of statistics and the connotation of machine learning.
cues.zh: 但有點像統計與機器學習兩種名稱所帶含意的差異。

cues.en: With statistics, we're trying to use existing data to explain something, some new phenomenon.
cues.zh: 統計想用現有資料，解釋某些新現象。

cues.en: And with machine learning, we're often trying to use available data to make predictions about something else.
cues.zh: 機器學習則常用可取得的資料，預測其他東西。

cues.en: So you can see that when people say statistics and when people say machine learning, they're often not really very different from each other.
cues.zh: 所以人們說統計與機器學習時，兩者往往並沒有非常不同。

cues.en: They're just kind of two different perspectives.
cues.zh: 只是兩種不同觀點。

cues.en: So if you would flip these around and try to use how much money people are spending on food to predict how much they slept last night, that doesn't change the overall statistics.
cues.zh: 如果反過來，用買食物花費預測昨晚睡眠，不會改變整體統計結果。

cues.en: Obviously it's going to change the individual beta regressors because you're swapping around the terms, but the model is essentially the same.
cues.zh: 當然，交換項目會改變個別 beta 迴歸係數，但模型本質上相同。

cues.en: We're really just swapping X and Y over here.
cues.zh: 只是交換這裡的 X 與 Y。

cues.en: So that said, the point of that is that you should set up your statistical models however way makes most sense for the question that you are asking for the research
cues.zh: 重點是，統計模型應以最符合研究問題，

cues.en: that you are trying to do.
cues.zh: 以及想做的研究的方式設定。

cues.en: So here is our design matrix, the beta coefficients and the observed data.
cues.zh: 這是設計矩陣、beta 係數，以及觀察資料。

cues.en: So I ran this model and it turns out that the intercept is 63 and the beta coefficient beta one is minus 2.5.
cues.zh: 執行模型後，截距是 63，beta1 係數是負 2.5。

cues.en: So these are the answers, but what do these mean?
cues.zh: 這些是答案，但代表什麼？

cues.en: What is even the scale of these data?
cues.zh: 這些資料的尺度究竟是什麼？

cues.en: So to understand what these mean, we're gonna move to visualization again.
cues.zh: 要理解意義，再回到視覺化。

cues.en: So we're gonna go back and let's see.
cues.zh: 回去看看。

cues.en: So this is the, the model.
cues.zh: 這是模型。

cues.en: So now I'm just putting in those beta terms here.
cues.zh: 現在把 beta 項代入。

cues.en: So YI, so the IF data point equals 63 minus 2.5
cues.zh: 第 i 個資料點 Yᵢ，等於 63 減 2.5，

cues.en: times xxi plus epsilon.
cues.zh: 乘 Xᵢ，再加 epsilon。

cues.en: Okay? So that's actually our equation. And here's the data.
cues.zh: 這就是方程式，這裡是資料。

cues.en: So here you see the observed data, this you already saw, and here we have the model prediction.
cues.zh: 觀察資料先前看過，這裡是模型預測。

cues.en: So this is the model predicted values here, they all lie on this line.
cues.zh: 模型預測值全都落在這條線上。

cues.en: And then we have the residuals, which is the epsilons.
cues.zh: 接著是殘差，也就是 epsilon。

cues.en: And what I'm drawing for you here is the distance of the epsilons to the model.
cues.zh: 這裡畫出 epsilon 相對於模型的距離。

cues.en: Now, the reason why the fitting procedure for the GLM for the regression is called lease squares, is that that solution, that lease squares solution
cues.zh: GLM、迴歸的擬合程序之所以叫最小平方法，是因為那個最小平方解，

cues.en: with the left inverse that I showed in a couple videos ago, that solution guarantees that these squared distances, so the squared epsilons are as small
cues.zh: 也就是幾支影片之前展示、使用左反矩陣的解，保證這些平方距離，也就是 epsilon 平方，

cues.en: as they possibly can be.
cues.zh: 會盡可能小。

cues.en: So the collection of squared epsilons cannot possibly be smaller than what they are with this best fit line, which is the model.
cues.zh: 這些 epsilon 平方的總體，不可能比最佳擬合線，也就是模型所得到的更小。

cues.en: And that's given to us by the lee squares equation.
cues.zh: 這就是最小平方方程式給我們的結果。

cues.en: So multiplying the data by the left inverse of the design matrix.
cues.zh: 以設計矩陣的左反矩陣乘上資料。

cues.en: So let's talk about a few things here.
cues.zh: 談幾件事。

cues.en: So first of all, we have this intercept.
cues.zh: 首先是截距。

cues.en: This intercept is in dollars, Fijian dollars.
cues.zh: 截距的單位是元，斐濟元。

cues.en: And remember that this intercept tells us where the data across the y axis, when the x axis or when all the parameters are set to zero.
cues.zh: 記住，截距告訴我們，X 或其他所有參數設為 0 時，資料穿過 Y 軸的位置。

cues.en: So when, when xxi is set to zero, then the prediction is that the Y axis is 63.
cues.zh: Xᵢ 設為 0，模型預測 Y 軸值為 63。

cues.en: Now what does that mean in this context?
cues.zh: 在這個脈絡中，代表什麼？

cues.en: The intercept in this context means that the prediction, the model prediction is that when someone sleeps zero hours last night,
cues.zh: 這個截距表示模型預測，若某人前一晚完全沒有睡覺，

cues.en: then today they're going to spend $63 on food.
cues.zh: 今天就會花 63 元買食物。

cues.en: And that's because notice that this x axis here stops at four.
cues.zh: 注意，這裡的 X 軸只到 4。

cues.en: So if we would continue this line all the way up to where X goes to zero, then this line would cross x equals zero at y equals 63.
cues.zh: 如果把線一路延伸到 X 為 0，會在 Y 等於 63 時通過 X 等於 0。

cues.en: Now we can ask the question of whether that makes sense.
cues.zh: 可以問，這合理嗎？

cues.en: Do we want to interpret this intercept?
cues.zh: 要解讀這個截距嗎？

cues.en: It's kind of a weird concept to think about, you know, predicting spending $63 when someone slept zero hours the previous night.
cues.zh: 預測某人昨晚睡 0 小時，會花 63 元，是有點奇怪的概念。

cues.en: I don't think that this is really interpretable.
cues.zh: 我認為不太能解讀。

cues.en: In my opinion, the intercept here is only included to make sure that we can get this best fit line off of the intercept.
cues.zh: 我認為這裡納入截距，只是為了讓最佳擬合線能離開原點。

cues.en: If we didn't have an intercept in this term, then this best fit line would be forced to go through zero zero.
cues.zh: 沒有截距，最佳擬合線就必須通過 0、0。

cues.en: So then the best fit line would look something like this.
cues.zh: 會像這樣。

cues.en: Okay, so that's the intercept.
cues.zh: 這是截距。

cues.en: Here we have the regression coefficient, which we can call a slope for a simple regression.
cues.zh: 這是迴歸係數，在簡單迴歸中可以稱為斜率。

cues.en: So that is minus 2.5.
cues.zh: 值為負 2.5。

cues.en: So that tells us that for every extra hour, so for every one unit on the x axis,
cues.zh: 表示每多一小時，也就是 X 軸每增加一個單位，

cues.en: we go down 2.5 units on the Y axis.
cues.zh: Y 軸就下降 2.5 個單位。

cues.en: In other words, for every extra hour that we sleep, we are going to spend $2 and 50 cents less on food the next day.
cues.zh: 換句話說，每多睡一小時，隔天買食物就少花 2 元 50 分。

cues.en: Again, that every single person will follow exactly this pattern.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，每個人都會精確遵循這個模式。

cues.en: You can see there's quite some individual variability.
cues.zh: 可以看到，有不少個體變異。

cues.en: This is telling us that the model predicts that on average for everyone, for this sample, every extra hour that you sleep, every unit on the x axis gives you
cues.zh: 這表示模型預測，平均而言，對這份樣本中的所有人，每多睡一小時，也就是 X 軸一個單位，

cues.en: minus 0.25 on the Y axis.
cues.zh: Y 軸會減少 0.25。

cues.en: Okay, so here's some of these statistics about this model.
cues.zh: 這裡是模型的一些統計量。

cues.en: So I found that the R squared is 0.36.
cues.zh: R 平方是 0.36。

cues.en: The F statistic, which has one and eight degrees of freedom was 4.5.
cues.zh: F 統計量的自由度是 1 與 8，值為 4.5。

cues.en: Now this sounds like a pretty decently sized F ratio or F statistic, but it turned out that the P value was only 0.066.
cues.zh: 聽起來是不錯的 F 比值，但 P 值其實只有 0.066。

cues.en: So in fact, despite what our visual intuition was telling us about this relationship, we cannot conclude that there is a significant effect of sleep on the amount
cues.zh: 因此，儘管視覺直覺認為有關係，仍無法下結論，說睡眠對人們買食物所花

cues.en: of money that people are spending on food.
cues.zh: 金額有顯著影響。

cues.en: So this would be a marginally significant result.
cues.zh: 這算邊緣顯著的結果。

cues.en: It's greater than 0.05, less than 0.1.
So we would call this marginally significant.
cues.zh: 因此稱為邊緣顯著。

cues.en: Now that may seem a little bit counterintuitive because visually it certainly looks like this is a pretty clear negative relationship between these two variables.
cues.zh: 可能有點違反直覺，因為視覺上，兩個變數似乎有很清楚的負向關係。

cues.en: But let's see.
cues.zh: 不過，看看。

cues.en: This may actually be due to a small sample size.
cues.zh: 其實可能是樣本太小。

cues.en: So what I tried to do after I ran this model with the data, I took the exact same parameters here, so the same intercept and the same slope.
cues.zh: 執行模型之後，我取完全相同參數，也就是相同截距與斜率，

cues.en: And I reevaluated the F statistic with updated degrees of freedom, denominated degrees of freedom, basically just assuming that we had 40 participants.
cues.zh: 更新自由度、分母自由度，基本上假設有 40 位參與者，再評估 F 統計量。

cues.en: So in this thought experiment, I had found exactly the same relationship, exactly the same findings, but with an N of 40 instead of an N of 10.
cues.zh: 這個思想實驗，是完全相同關係與發現，只是 N 從 10 改成 40。

cues.en: And then that lowered the P value to 0.039, which of course would be considered statistically significant.
cues.zh: 如此 P 值降到 0.039，當然就會視為統計顯著。

cues.en: So this is just an illustration of the importance of sample size.
cues.zh: 這只是示範樣本大小的重要性。

cues.en: If you have a really small sample size, you are likely to get a non-significant F statistic, even if the effect is really there in the population.
cues.zh: 樣本非常小時，即使母體真的有效果，也很可能得到不顯著的 F 統計量。

cues.en: So this relationship between the P value and N is something you've learned about already quite a bit in the TAs section and the section on correlation.
cues.zh: P 值與 N 的關係，在 t 檢定與相關單元，已經學過不少。

cues.en: Okay, so I hope you enjoyed this experiment and I hope you are enthusiastic about visiting Fiji at some point in the future.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡這個實驗，也對未來某天去斐濟感到期待。

cues.en: And I guess maybe more importantly, I hope you are a little bit more comfortable with thinking about regression and working through regression.
cues.zh: 也許更重要的是，希望你現在更能自在思考與處理迴歸。
